title: Google Merch Store Analytics Workspace
subtitle: Engineering an optimization dashboard in Looker Studio utilizing raw GA4 e-commerce schemas for retail performance auditing.
desc: A Looker Studio dashboard connected directly to the GA4 Google Merchandise Store property, tracking conversion funnels, item performance, and marketing attribution.
overview: Direct UI-to-UI native cloud connections often default to slow load speeds and cluttered visual spaces. This case study details the clean engineering of a retail-focused performance workspace, transforming public GA4 clickstream event parameters into actionable revenue tracking and performance scorecards.

sections.heading: The Analytical Challenge
sections.content: Modern digital retail platforms capture billions of event arrays. The primary engineering bottleneck isn't collecting data—it's mapping high-dimensional GA4 event parameters (like items, item_name, view_item, and purchase) into clean, low-latency business scorecards. This layout maps out the entire digital user journey across the Google Merchandise Store, keeping page load latency low through native component caching.

sections.heading: Conversion Architecture & Funnel Auditing
sections.content: The application leverages specific GA4 e-commerce schemas to build a strict linear progression pipeline. By isolating the 'view_item' -> 'add_to_cart' -> 'purchase' event flows, the dashboard maps visual conversion walls. This instantly lets stakeholders detect drop-off friction points, isolate lower-performing item categories, and track cross-channel marketing attribution models cleanly.

title: Automated Multi-Channel Marketing Ingestion Pipeline
subtitle: Orchestrating a serverless, metadata-driven ETL engine on GCP to aggregate custom marketing API telemetry with raw GA4 conversion exports.
desc: A decoupled, configuration-driven data engineering pipeline built to circumvent endpoint licensing costs, utilizing BigQuery views to calculate exact cross-platform cost-per-conversion and judge campaign performance.

meta.stack: GCP, Cloud Functions, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Looker Studio

overview: Siloed marketing networks make unified ROI tracking manual and expensive, while commercial ETL tools impose strict pricing walls based on the number of active endpoints. This architecture circumvents scaling costs entirely by decoupling the ingestion logic from API metadata. Python Cloud Functions pull spend telemetry dynamically using endpoint schemas stored in Google Cloud Storage, while a native GA4 BigQuery export streams conversion arrays daily to compute exact cost-per-conversion metrics.

sections.heading: Metadata-Driven Architecture & Cost Circumvention
sections.content: Traditional ingestion setups require hardcoded functions for every new API connector, and commercial solutions penalize growth by charging per endpoint. To solve this, this pipeline uses a completely metadata-driven approach: the Cloud Functions act as generic, highly reusable workers that merely execute requests. All sensitive API credentials, configuration objects, target endpoints, and metric dimensions are stored as decoupled JSON payloads inside secure Google Cloud Storage buckets. Scaling to a new marketing API requires zero code deployment—only a new config object in storage.

sections.heading: Unified Conversion Attribution Logic
sections.content:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW `marketing_analytics.unified_performance_attribution` AS
WITH aggregated_spend AS (
  SELECT date, 'Facebook' AS channel, campaign_name, cost FROM `fb.daily_spend`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date, 'TikTok' AS channel, campaign_name, cost FROM `tiktok.daily_spend`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date, 'Google' AS channel, campaign_name, cost FROM `google.daily_spend` 
),
ga4_conversions AS (
  SELECT 
    parse_date('%Y%m%d', _table_suffix) AS date,
    lower(traffic_source.source) AS channel,
    traffic_source.name AS campaign_name,
    count(distinct user_pseudo_id) AS total_conversions
  FROM `ga4_export.events_*` 
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
SELECT 
  s.date,
  s.channel,
  s.campaign_name,
  sum(s.cost) AS total_ad_spend,
  sum(c.total_conversions) AS conversion_count,
  safe_divide(sum(s.cost), sum(c.total_conversions)) AS cost_per_conversion
FROM aggregated_spend s
LEFT JOIN ga4_conversions c 
  ON s.date = c.date 
  AND lower(s.channel) = c.channel
  AND lower(s.campaign_name) = lower(c.campaign_name)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;

sections.heading: Judging Campaign Performance via GA4 Web Data
sections.content: Relying on ad network pixels often results in distorted attribution due to self-reported success metrics. This workspace pulls raw GA4 clickstream event parameters as the absolute ground truth for campaign performance evaluation. By blending independent network spend datasets directly with GA4's downstream web transaction data inside BigQuery, stakeholders can analyze exact cost-per-conversion rates at the granular campaign level—ensuring marketing budgets are judged strictly on verified revenue outcomes.
